# Ebenezer Tarubinga

> Ebenezer Tarubinga, AI/ML research engineer in Seoul. Four first-author papers on semi-supervised semantic segmentation, and production LLM systems: hybrid RAG, tool-using agents, model routing and edge vision.

01 — Building
### Systems
Production and platform work is described by what it does and what I built, not by whose data is in it, so those repositories stay private.
### Hybrid retrieval over utility-operations data
Hybrid retrieval combining lexical and vector retrieval, reranking and knowledge-graph reasoning to produce evidence-backed answers. Retrieval quality is evaluated on a held-out set.
### Read-only operations agent for water-grid workflows
A read-only, tool-calling operations agent for water-grid workflows, with guardrails at tool boundaries and an adversarial-input evaluation harness.
### Road-infrastructure digital twin
Hardened a live road-infrastructure digital twin built with Three.js and PostGIS, taking a prototype toward certification.
### Multi-provider LLM routing
Implemented multi-provider LLM routing with circuit-breaker failover.
### Edge vision on municipal camera hardware
Deployed YOLOv5/OpenVINO detection to municipal camera hardware, with MQTT/serial integration and offline-first recovery.
### 10-database PostgreSQL fleet behind PgBouncer
Consolidated a 10-database PostgreSQL fleet behind PgBouncer, and traced a recurring ORM workload that read 54,000 rows every five minutes to compute eight status flags.
### OIDC identity and subscription gating
Built OIDC identity and subscription-gating components for a multi-product platform.
### Backdoor attacks on CLIP
Stealthy backdoor triggers via dual-embedding alignment in CLIP's joint visual and textual space, reproducing and extending BadCLIP.
### Semantic-aware multi-label adversarial attacks
Targeted perturbations for multi-label classifiers that exploit semantic label co-occurrence instead of treating each label independently.
### Semi-supervised segmentation baselines
A systematic evaluation of weak-to-strong consistency (UniMatch) and self-training (ST++).
### Monocular depth estimation
Depth and point-cloud generation for autonomous driving on KITTI, over an improved depth-to-pointcloud pipeline on Depth Anything V2.
### LLM evaluation: effective context length study
Reproduced and extended STRING-style analysis across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen2-7B. Evaluated RULER-style retrieval/tracking tasks at 4K–32K context lengths and analyzed RoPE positional decay and attention sinks; repository reports effective lengths of approximately 6K, 14K, 11K and 18K respectively.
### AgriLet, crop disease detection
Disease identification with severity scoring for smallholder farmers, plus learning modules, community data contributions and downloadable datasets.
### eLearn, an e-learning platform
O Level and A Level revision for African high-school students: 20+ subjects, 70+ lessons, study streaks and a learning-analytics dashboard.
02 — Research
### Papers
Four first-author papers on semi-supervised semantic segmentation: pseudo-label reliability, uncertainty calibration and contrastive learning, on CNN and DINOv2 backbones.
Research topics
### CW-BASS: Confidence-Weighted Boundary-Aware Learning for Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
Ebenezer Tarubinga, Jenifer Kalafatovich, Seong-Whan Lee
IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), 2025 · DOI 10.1109/IJCNN64981.2025.11227871
A confidence-weighted pseudo-label loss, adaptive thresholding and Sobel boundary supervision, targeting confirmation bias, noisy pseudo-labels and limited-label learning.
65.9 mIoU on Cityscapes with 100 labeled images (1/30)
### FARCLUSS: Fuzzy Adaptive Rebalancing and Contrastive Uncertainty Learning for Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
Ebenezer Tarubinga, Jenifer Kalafatovich, Seong-Whan Lee
Neural Networks, vol. 205, article 109494 (2027) · DOI 10.1016/j.neunet.2026.109494
Top-K fuzzy labels, entropy-based uncertainty weighting, adaptive class rebalancing and a 128-D prototype-contrastive head, with ResNet-101 at 1/8 labeled data.
78.2 mIoU on Pascal VOC and 78.5 on Cityscapes
### CW-BASS v2: Saturation-Aware Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Segmentation under Foundation-Model Teachers
Ebenezer Tarubinga
arXiv: 2608.12773 (2026)
A reliability gate for pseudo-label selection, evaluated across six DINOv2 teacher settings with 5% held-out calibration, on DINOv2-Base (ViT-B/14) with DPT-lite.
Pascal VOC 1/8: 86.19 ± 1.82 mIoU (3 seeds) · Cityscapes 83.96 and ADE20K 50.58 (+1.5 over the strict-threshold reproduction)
### PixCon: Clean-Positive Contrastive Learning for Foundation-Model Semi-Supervised Segmentation
Ebenezer Tarubinga
arXiv: 2607.03068 (2026) · under review
A clean-positive pixel-contrastive branch with 256 entries per class and τ=0.1. The contrastive head is training-only and adds no inference-time parameters.
Pascal VOC 1/8: 87.90 mIoU (3-seed mean, versus 87.01 for the matched reproduction) · Cityscapes 83.88 and ADE20K 49.23 (single-seed results)
Research highlights and experimental scale
### MSc research: CW-BASS and FARCLUSS
DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50/101 on Pascal VOC 2012 and Cityscapes; evaluated 1/16–1/2 labeled-data splits. CW-BASS combines confidence-weighted pseudo-label loss, adaptive thresholding and Sobel boundary supervision, reaching 65.9 mIoU on Cityscapes with 100 labeled images (1/30). FARCLUSS combines top-K fuzzy labels, entropy-based uncertainty weighting, adaptive class rebalancing and a 128-D prototype-contrastive head; ResNet-101 at 1/8 labeled data: 78.2 mIoU on VOC and 78.5 on Cityscapes. Training recipes: 80 epochs (VOC), 240 (Cityscapes), batch 4/2; CUDA multi-GPU DataParallel support in CW-BASS.
### Independent foundation-model research: CW-BASS v2 and PixCon
DINOv2-Base (ViT-B/14) with DPT-lite on Pascal VOC, Cityscapes and ADE20K. CW-BASS v2: 518×518 crops, 60 epochs, batch 4, AdamW, BF16 AMP, 5% held-out calibration and a reliability gate evaluated across six DINOv2 teacher settings. Pascal VOC 1/8: 86.19 ± 1.82 mIoU (3 seeds); Cityscapes 83.96 and ADE20K 50.58 (+1.5 over the strict-threshold reproduction). PixCon: 60/120-epoch recipes, batch 4 (effective 16 with gradient accumulation), clean-positive pixel-contrastive branch with 256 entries/class and τ=0.1. Pascal VOC 1/8: 87.90 mIoU (3-seed mean, versus 87.01 for the matched reproduction); Cityscapes 83.88 and ADE20K 49.23 (single-seed results). The contrastive head is training-only and adds no inference-time parameters.
03 — Released
### Open source
Selected open-source engineering, plus the code behind each paper.
Pure-Python HWP/HWPX document reader and editor; extracts Korean document text for retrieval pipelines and supports form filling and binary-safe rewriting. Published on PyPI.
Local-first Codex usage and token analytics with response-level deduplication, quota forensics and a terminal/dashboard interface; README reports scanning 1.85 GB of logs across 59 sessions in about 2 seconds on the development machine.
Dependency-free Python utilities for switching Claude Code and OpenAI Codex accounts or provider profiles across terminals.
A framework for personal and academic websites: typed section blocks, ORCID and BibTeX ingestion, and a licence that leaves the owner holding their own copy.
Code for each of the four papers.

07 — Questions
### Questions
### What does Ebenezer Tarubinga do?
AI/ML engineer and first-author researcher working across dense prediction and production LLM systems. Research spans semi-supervised semantic segmentation, pseudo-label reliability, uncertainty calibration and contrastive learning; engineering work spans hybrid RAG, knowledge-graph retrieval, tool-using agents, multi-provider model routing and edge vision.
### What is his current role?
AI/ML Engineer at Gractor in Seoul, Korea, since September 2025. I built hybrid retrieval for utility-operations data, a read-only tool-calling operations agent for water-grid workflows, multi-provider LLM routing with circuit-breaker failover and YOLOv5/OpenVINO edge detection, and hardened a road-infrastructure digital twin.
### What does his research cover?
Four first-author papers on semi-supervised semantic segmentation: CW-BASS (IEEE IJCNN 2025), FARCLUSS (Neural Networks, vol. 205), CW-BASS v2 (arXiv:2608.12773) and PixCon (arXiv:2607.03068, under review). The first two are MSc research at Korea University; the last two are independent research.
### What is CW-BASS v2?
A first-author paper on saturation-aware pseudo-label selection under foundation-model teachers (arXiv:2608.12773, 2026). It uses DINOv2-Base (ViT-B/14) with DPT-lite and a reliability gate evaluated across six DINOv2 teacher settings, and reaches 86.19 ± 1.82 mIoU on Pascal VOC 1/8 over three seeds.
### What is PixCon?
A first-author paper on clean-positive contrastive learning for foundation-model semi-supervised segmentation (arXiv:2607.03068, 2026), under review. The contrastive head is training-only and adds no inference-time parameters. On Pascal VOC 1/8 it reaches 87.90 mIoU (3-seed mean, versus 87.01 for the matched reproduction).
### What has he released as open source?
hwpkit: a pure-Python HWP/HWPX document reader and editor, published on PyPI. codexwatch: local-first Codex usage and token analytics. claudehop and codexhop: dependency-free Python utilities for switching Claude Code and OpenAI Codex accounts or provider profiles across terminals. Also tzohar-engine, a framework for personal and academic websites, and the code for the four papers.
### What did he study and research at Korea University?
An MSc in Artificial Intelligence, 2023–2026, GPA 3.78/4.0, advised by Prof. Seong-Whan Lee (IEEE Fellow). I was a Research Engineer in the Pattern Recognition & Machine Learning Lab from August 2023 to August 2025, hold the Global Korea Scholarship (sole Zimbabwean awardee) and a BK21 Research Fellowship, and contributed to a Korean patent application for real-time object detection.
### Is he open to new work?
Open to ML and research-engineer roles, and to research collaborations.
### Let's build something that ships.
Open to ML and research-engineer roles, and to research collaborations.
